key_insight: Diagnostic accuracy alone can hide whether a medical LLM actually used the right evidence, so the paper audits evidence use rather than just final answers.
clinical_relevance: This matters because models may appear reliable while relying on shortcuts, missing negations, or clinically implausible cues that could affect diagnosis support.
method: Decomposed each patient case into evidence units and tested diagnoses under controlled evidence subsets.
Mined low-order interactions in diagnostic margins to see how different evidence pieces change model choices.
Separated clinically plausible differential-diagnosis effects from suspicious shortcut-like failures using robustness checks and clinical review.
evidence_signal: Across DDXPlus, CupCase, and MedCase, faithful support plus differential conflict or cancellation explained most interaction strength, while a blinded 130-item DDXPlus review found invalid or shortcut-like cases concentrated in negated/absent findings and local evidence.
watch_item: Interaction patterns are diagnosis-relative, so some large effects are not errors; interpreting them requires careful clinical validation before drawing conclusions about model failure.
paper_title: Auditing Evidence Use in Medical LLM Diagnosis
